candidate_records.name: Bryans Master Cobbler
candidate_records.description: Terraced three-bay four-storey house, built c.1840, now in commercial use with rented accommodation over, having shopfront and integral carriage arch. Flat roof with shared red brick chimneystacks to east party wall behind red brick parapet wall having masonry coping. Red brick wall laid in Flemish bond with red brick soldier quoins to east of façade. Render wall to ground floor to east of shopfront with moulded masonry cornice over. Diminishing gauged brick square-headed window openings with masonry sills and replacement uPVC windows throughout. Recent timber shopfront to ground floor comprising engaged pilasters on plinth bases having applied mirrored strips, pedimented consoles flanking fascia over square-headed opening. Segmental-arch carriage entrance to east of shopfront with recent single-leaf metal sheet door.
candidate_records.appraisal: Forms part of a relatively uniform terrace with shared parapet height and fenestration pattern. Its carriage arch provides access to the rear of the site.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010213 present in the workflow-generated Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.name: Iskender Burger Hut
candidate_records.description: Terraced two-bay four-storey house, built c.1840, now in commercial use with accommodation over, having recent shopfront to ground floor. Flat roof with shared red brick chimneystack to west party wall behind red brick parapet wall having masonry coping. Red brick wall laid in Flemish bond with red brick soldier quoins to west of façade. Diminishing gauged brick square-headed window openings with masonry sills and replacement uPVC windows throughout. Timber shopfront to ground floor comprising engaged panelled pilasters on plinth bases having moulded string course and shaped consoles, flanking fascia with moulded render architrave over recent square-headed glazed windows and door openings. Square-headed door opening to east of shopfront with steel shutters over.
candidate_records.appraisal: Part of the relatively uniform terrace lining the north side of Talbot Street, sharing parapet height, fenestration pattern and regularity of design and proportion.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010214 present in the workflow-generated Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.description: Terraced two-bay four-storey house, built c.1840, now in use as commercial outlet, having recent shopfront to ground floor. Pitched slate roof with shared red brick chimneystack to east party wall behind rendered parapet wall with masonry coping. Cast-iron hopper to top of façade. Lined-and-ruled rendered wall with panelled render engaged pilaster to east of façade. Diminishing square-headed window openings with masonry sills, moulded masonry shouldered-and-kneed architrave surrounds and replacement uPVC windows to second and third floors. Square-headed window openings having masonry sills, surrounds and moulded masonry pediments on scrolled consoles with foliate designs to first floor windows. Recent shopfront to ground floor comprising engaged pilasters on plinth bases, plain fascia over recent square-headed glazed window and door openings.
candidate_records.appraisal: The rendered façade is enlivened by moulded window surrounds, especially the pedimented hood-mouldings to the first floor, and panelled render pilasters; it contrasts with the predominantly red-brick terrace.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010215 present in the workflow-generated Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.address: 1 Talbot Street / Marlborough Street corner, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.description: Corner-sited end-of-terrace two-bay four-storey house, built c.1840, having shopfront to ground floor. Pitched slate roof, hipped to southwest corner, with shared red brick chimneystacks to north and east party walls behind parapet wall having granite coping. Red brick walls laid in Flemish bond with red brick engaged pilaster to north of west elevation, having rounded finial on square plinth to top. Diminishing gauged brick segmental-headed window openings with masonry sills, chamfered reveals and single-pane timber sliding sash windows. Two-tier shopfront to south and west elevations, comprising timber pilasters on plinth bases having pedimented capitals, flanking timber fascia and moulded cornice over replacement uPVC windows to first floor. Recent shopfront to ground floor with square-profile pilasters supporting fascia over square-headed glazed openings.
candidate_records.appraisal: Prominently sited at the junction of Talbot Street and Marlborough Street; retains part of the parapet height and fenestration rhythm, with segmental-headed openings and timber sash windows adding interest.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010216 present in the workflow-generated Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.description: Terraced three-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1800. Double-pile slate roof, with pair of hipped projections to rear. Roof hidden behind parapet wall with granite coping and rendered chimneystack with clay pots rising from north gable. Further chimneystack rising from rear elevation with clay pots. Red brick walls laid in Flemish bond on chamfered granite plinth course over rendered basement walls. Walls rebuilt to top two floors. Ruled-and-lined cement rendered walls to north gable and return having stone cornice to parapet and cast-iron rainwater goods. Gauged brick flat-arch window openings with rendered reveals, granite sills and replacement timber sash windows throughout. Tripartite window openings to north elevation of return at each level with granite mullions on granite sills with mouldings to plain granite frieze and cornice. Wrought-iron grilles to basement windows. Round-headed door opening with decorative coved surround and painted masonry Ionic doorcase. Replacement timber panelled door flanked by engaged Ionic columns on plinth blocks supported fluted stepped lintel cornice with decorative webbed leaded fanlight over.
candidate_records.appraisal: An elegant Georgian house recently restored to a high standard. Its decorative doorcase and tripartite windows add interest, and it terminates the north end of a short terrace.

duplicate_screen.method: Exact registration-number searches against the repository's official-register reconciliation results, open issues and pull requests.
duplicate_screen.result: No existing archive register matches and no open issue or pull request matches returned for these five exact registration numbers at time of research.

identity_and_spatial_cautions: The five NIAH registrations identify five separate buildings; retain each registration as a separate building entity.
Nos.3A and 3A Talbot Street (50010213 and 50010214) are separate registrations with different building descriptions and façades. Do not collapse them because their address number is shared.
The NIAH national CSV has a blank NAME field for 50010215, 50010216 and 50010219. Their addresses and registration numbers are retained; no business or building name is invented.
Registration 50010216 is described as a corner-sited building at Talbot Street and Marlborough Street. Preserve its corner relationship without creating a duplicate street address.
Registration 50010219 is 28 Marlborough Street and its NIAH record notes a relationship/abutment with the former National Model Schools campus. It remains a separate registration.
NIAH names, uses and condition descriptions are survey-time source statements and do not verify present-day tenant, occupancy, ownership, public access or condition.
Raw individual-page coordinate pairs are preserved separately from official CSV ITM and latitude/longitude values. Do not mix coordinate systems.
